item.text: I found a meaningful remaining design issue: stats, colors, and dashboard grouping still key off Java classes instead of first-class species descriptors. I’m refactoring that layer so actors expose a public type descriptor and the UI/stats code depends on species metadata instead of runtime class identity.
I’m pushing the stats/UI layer off raw class identity now. Actors will expose a first-class type descriptor, and counters/colors/dashboard grouping will use that instead of `Class<?>` keys.
The type-descriptor layer is in. I still need to finish the dashboard loops and then recompile against updated stubs so the UI-facing signatures line up with the new `ActorType` keys.
I’m continuing from the last structural pass by finishing the `ActorType` migration and then scanning for the remaining class-keyed code paths so the refactor lands cleanly.
I’ve confirmed the remaining breakage is isolated to `Dashboard.java`. I’m going to finish that migration and use the opportunity to collapse the duplicated chart-building logic there.

I’m editing `Dashboard.java` now to remove the remaining `Class`-based logic and to consolidate the duplicated population/vegetation chart code. After that I’ll drop the now-unused `getActorClass()` API from the species enums.
The `ActorType` migration is clean now. I’m doing one more cleanup pass in `Dashboard.java` to remove dead fields/import noise before compiling the refactored core.

I’ve finished the code edits. Next step is verification: first a targeted compile of the refactored simulation classes with the existing dashboard stub, then a quick search for stale APIs or type mismatches.

item.text:
I continued the refactor by finishing the move away from runtime `Class<?>` identity toward explicit actor descriptors.

The main design change is a first-class actor metadata layer in [ActorType.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/ActorType.java:1) and [ActorCategory.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/ActorCategory.java:1). `Animal` and `Plant` now expose their type through that interface, `AnimalSpecies` and `PlantSpecies` implement it directly, and the old unused `getActorClass()` plumbing was removed from both species enums. That lets stats, colors, and UI work off stable species metadata instead of Java class keys.

I also cleaned the consumers of that model: [FieldStats.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/FieldStats.java:1) now stores `Map<ActorType, Counter>`, [SimulatorView.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/SimulatorView.java:1) colors and renders by `ActorType`, and [Dashboard.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R006_module_java/Dashboard.java:1) no longer uses `Class` checks. While touching `Dashboard`, I also collapsed the duplicated animal/plant chart population logic into shared helpers.

Verification: the refactored simulation classes compile successfully with the existing dashboard stub:
```bash
javac -d /private/tmp/java-classes -sourcepath /private/tmp/java-stubs /private/tmp/java-stubs/Dashboard.java ...
```
Direct compilation of `Dashboard.java` still fails in this environment because JavaFX packages are not installed (`javafx.application`, `javafx.scene.*`, etc.); that is an environment/toolchain issue, not a new refactor regression.
